title: Human Islet Quantification and Purity Assessment
author: James Lyon
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bus3nwgn

steps.title: Prepare DMSO‑dithizone staining solution
steps.instruction: Weigh 0.2 g dithizone powder into a 50 mL conical tube, add 6 mL DMSO and mix until dissolved, then add HBSS to bring the volume to 40 mL, mix, and filter the solution through a 0.45 µm nylon filter into a 60 cc syringe.

steps.title: Add DTZ to islet suspension
steps.instruction: For each mL of islet suspension add an equal volume of the prepared DTZ solution; optionally add 2 mL HBSS to dilute the stain and reduce background. As an alternative, combine 50 µL islet suspension, 50 µL DTZ, and 2000 µL HBSS.

steps.title: Incubate until red staining appears
steps.instruction: Add approximately 1 mL DTZ to the sample (or the mixture prepared in step 2) and incubate at room temperature until the islets are visibly red; if needed add ~1 mL HBSS to further dilute background.

steps.title: Mount sample for microscopic counting
steps.instruction: Place the stained sample on the microscope stage and prepare to count islet equivalents (IEQ) in duplicate.

steps.title: Measure particle diameters with graticule
steps.instruction: Using an ocular graticule where one square equals 100 µm × 100 µm, measure the diameter (or circular equivalent) of each particle ≥ 50 µm, record each measurement in the appropriate column of the counting table; particles < 50 µm are excluded.

steps.title: Calculate column subtotals and total count
steps.instruction: After counting the entire sample, sum the values in each column and the overall total, entering the results into the table (step 11). For faster counting, a 9‑channel benchtop cell counter (Bal Supply, catalogue 808CI) may be used.

steps.title: Determine multiplication factor
steps.instruction: Calculate the multiplication factor by dividing the total volume of the suspension by the volume sampled (e.g., 100 mL / 0.050 mL = 2000 ×).

steps.title: Compute islet equivalents (IEQ)
steps.instruction: Multiply the total particle count by the multiplication factor to obtain the total islet equivalents; record the IEQ per size range as shown in the example tables.

steps.title: Estimate percent purity
steps.instruction: Estimate the ratio of islet area to exocrine tissue area and express it as a percentage (e.g., equal areas = 50 %).

steps.title: Estimate percent trapped islets
steps.instruction: Estimate the proportion of trapped islets relative to total islets and record it as a percentage.

steps.title: Score islet morphology
steps.instruction: Assess shape, border, integrity, presence of <25 µm islets, and clumping, assigning scores (0–3) according to the Islet Scoring Table; sum the scores to obtain the final islet score (e.g., 8).

steps.title: Calculate islet particle index (IPI)
steps.instruction: Sum all ‘Mean Count’ values, multiply by the multiplication factor to obtain total islet particles (IP); divide total islet equivalents by IP to get the islet particle index (IPI). An IPI < 1.0 indicates a smaller size distribution, > 1.0 indicates a larger distribution.
